study_identification_part.si4_title: Lifespan Normative Models of White Matter Fractional Anisotropy: Applications to Early Psychosis

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To develop large-scale lifespan normative models of white matter fractional anisotropy (FA) and apply them to an early psychosis cohort to quantify individual-level deviations, investigate heterogeneity, and identify multimodal (FA and structural) brain-symptom relationships.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: Human Connectome Project (HCP) Baby; HCP Development; HCP Young Adult; HCP Aging; UK Biobank
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper explicitly lists the five cohorts used to build the reference dataset.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: First, we assembled high-quality multi-shell diffusion data from five cohorts having closely matched acquisition and processing pipelines, namely Human Connectome Project (HCP) Baby [20], HCP Development [21], HCP Young Adult [22], HCP Aging [23] datasets, and UK Biobank [24].

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of mean deviations (t-tests with FDR correction); group comparisons of extreme deviation proportions (Mann-Whitney U test with FDR correction); multi-view sparse canonical correlation analysis (msCCA) to map symptom domains to multimodal (FA and structural) deviation profiles, with stability selection.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Lifespan normative models of fractional anisotropy reveal significant inter-individual heterogeneity in early psychosis, and multimodal deviations in FA and brain volume (thalamus, uncinate fasciculus) are predictive of clinical symptom severity.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Despite no significant group differences in mean FA deviations after FDR correction, individuals with psychosis showed significantly more extreme positive and negative deviations compared to controls. A multi-view sparse CCA revealed a significant relationship (r=0.25) between clinical symptoms (driven by cognitive and total PANSS scores) and multimodal brain deviations. Stability selection identified FA in the right uncinate fasciculus and bilateral thalamus volume as the most informative features predicting symptom severity.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The reference dataset has a skewed age distribution with fewer subjects at the extremes of lifespan (5-8 and >85 years). Demographic factors like socioeconomic background were not explored. The training data is biased towards 'WEIRD' populations and self-reported race is an imperfect proxy for ethnicity.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: The age distribution in our dataset is skewed, with fewer data points at the extremes of the lifespan... variability due to demographic factors like socioeconomic background was not fully explored... the datasets on which these models were trained on are not representative of the wider population and are themselves biased towards 'Western Educated, Industrialised, Rich and Democratic' (WEIRD) populations... Self-reported race is also an imperfect proxy for ethnicity...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: A multi-view sparse CCA (msCCA) was used to integrate deviation scores from different imaging modalities (dMRI FA, sMRI cortical thickness, sMRI subcortical volume) to predict multiple clinical symptom domains simultaneously. Generalizability was assessed using stability selection over 1000 random train/test splits rather than nested cross-validation for parameter tuning.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: All normative models developed in this study are made publicly available through open-source software platforms (PCNtoolkit and a dedicated GitHub repository).
